title: Present In Both Systems
description:
Report every `order_id` that appears in **both** `source_orders` and `warehouse_orders`.

Name the column `order_id`. Return the result in any order.
hint: INTERSECT keeps only rows present in both SELECTs — exactly "in both systems".
outputExplanation: Only order ids 1 and 2 appear in both systems. Orders 3 and 4 are source-only and order 5 is warehouse-only.

tests.name: Example
All three systems fully agree
Completely disjoint across all three
Source has an accidental duplicate row
Only source has any data
tests.seedSql: INSERT INTO source_orders VALUES (1,'Ann Lee',120.0),(2,'Ben Kim',80.0),(3,'Cy Ortiz',45.5);

tests.name: Same order, inconsistent name formatting
Matching ids, mismatched amounts
Single matching order everywhere
Larger mixed set: some in all three, some in two, some in one, duplicates and a mismatch
No overlap at all — disjoint tables
tests.seedSql:
INSERT INTO source_orders VALUES (1,'A',100.0),(2,'B',200.0);
INSERT INTO warehouse_orders VALUES (3,'C',300.0),(4,'D',400.0);

tests.name: All rows overlap — identical data
tests.seedSql:
INSERT INTO source_orders VALUES (1,'A',100.0),(2,'B',200.0);
INSERT INTO warehouse_orders VALUES (1,'A',100.0),(2,'B',200.0);

tests.name: Partial overlap
tests.seedSql:
INSERT INTO source_orders VALUES (1,'A',100.0),(2,'B',200.0),(3,'C',300.0);
INSERT INTO warehouse_orders VALUES (2,'B',200.0),(3,'C',300.0),(4,'D',400.0);

tests.name: Duplicates in source table
tests.seedSql:
INSERT INTO source_orders VALUES (1,'A',100.0),(1,'A',100.0),(2,'B',200.0);
INSERT INTO warehouse_orders VALUES (1,'A',100.0);
